ledger.hypothesis: at 120 points the arithmetic is negligible; the 18 us is dominated by MFnNurbsCurveData::create + MFnNurbsCurve::create (allocation, knot validation, internal curve build) and by ~10 shared_ptr<vector> temporaries plus a 122-append MDoubleArray knot rebuild per tick. Fusing the chain removes the temporaries (measured 0.0174 -> 0.0116 ms); writing CVs into the existing output data object removes the curve rebuild (measured 0.0116 -> 0.0033 ms). Every CV is recomputed every tick; only the container is reused, guarded on numCVs/degree/form/numKnots and falling back to create().

ledger.theme: the helix is 120 CVs with fixed topology, so refill the previous tick's kNurbsCurveData with setCVs+updateCurve instead of creating a fresh curve object every evaluation, and fuse the numpy chain into one allocation-free loop over constant u / knot tables built once in the constructor

ledger.hypothesis: At 120 CVs the compute is ~1.9 us of call overhead, not arithmetic: 120 out-of-line MPointArray::set calls (~300 ns) plus a six-call hasFn/ctor/numCVs/degree/form/numKnots re-validation of the same data object every tick (~350 ns) are a third of it, while the exact sincos loop (~300 ns) and setCVs+updateCurve (~450 ns) are the floor the public API allows. Removing whole calls, not cheapening the math, is the lever; every input moves to a fresh value each tick so no input-keyed cache can hit.
ledger.risk: MPointArray contiguity is asserted once at construction (last-first address == 119 * sizeof(MPoint), every element address checked, w == 1.0 after an explicit init) and falls back to per-element set() otherwise; the bound MFnNurbsCurve is re-validated only when the plug hands back a different MObject, with a failed setCVs dropping to the full create path. Official geo parity on the built .mll: maxerr 0.0 (bit-identical). In-compute steady_clock timers (diagnostic build, removed) showed 1.9 -> 1.3 us per tick; the harness median fell 3.0 -> 2.5 us on a quiet run, but five sibling mayapy processes on this machine swing single medians between 2.5 and 5.5 us, so a single driver measurement may not resolve the gain. An interleaved A/B under identical load (handed-in baseline built into a separate directory, runs alternated) read baseline 5.2 / 5.1 / 5.2 us vs optimized 4.3 / 4.2 / 4.1 us, i.e. ~1.22x, matching the quiet pair. Not attempted on purpose: any algebraic restructuring of the 120 sincos (angle-addition tables, rotation recurrence) -- it would trade the current bit-identical result for a 1-100 ULP one to save ~200 ns, which the harness cannot resolve. Windows note: the workspace build.sh/bench.sh are the macOS recipe and cannot run here; measurements used an MSVC twin with the identical harness invocation (same spec, --iters 9, --bench-array 20000, --bench-geo 400).
ledger.theme: Fill the reused CV buffer through a contiguity-proven raw MPoint pointer and keep the output curve's function set bound across evaluations, so one tick makes about ten Maya calls instead of about 135.
